90.t: Billy Berg's club and Slim Gaillard
90.s: Billy Berg's club, the Truville, Slim Gaillard's group, and nightly broadcasts with no cover.
90.ch: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
90.q: : Oh yeah, it was going really strong. It was located there at Longtree(?) and Vine. And he had also owned the Swing Club up on Hollywood Boulevard and Las Palmas, which I played -- later on I will talk about it.

90.t: Swing Club job opposite Scatman Crothers
90.s: The McGhee band in new uniforms alternates with Scatman Crothers's band at the Swing Club.
90.ch: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
90.q: And we were getting prepared to go on our big job, and we had worked and made a little money. So we had bought uniforms, and we had our light tan trousers and our brown jackets and everything, with our little neckties -- and we were sharp! We were going into Billy Berg's Swing Club.

90.t: George Bledsoe at the California Club
90.s: Singer-multi-instrumentalist George Bledsoe, whom RCA recorded in about 1948, and Bernie Peters.
90.ch: San Francisco and the postwar slump
90.q: And around San Francisco during that time, George Bledsoe was singing at a club called the California Club. That's where I first met him. And he's a great singer. He was playing piano and singing.

90.t: Illinois Jacquet and Calvin Jackson at the Swing Club
90.s: Meeting Illinois Jacquet, who tried to recruit him, and pianist Calvin Jackson sitting in.
90.ch: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
90.q: Going back to the Swing Club on Hollywood Boulevard and Las Palmas for a minute, because I have so many great memories from there. That's where I first met Illinois Jacquet. When I came here with Ernie Fields, he had his group with his brother Russell. They were playing. And he tried to persuade me…

418.t: Billy Berg's club and who played there
418.s: Morgenstern mentions Dickenson's band at Billy Berg's, where Hawkins, Dizzy and Charlie played.
418.ch: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
418.q: Probably, I don't know for sure whether they played there or not. I know -- I know Hawkins played there and Dizzy, Charlie, and quite a few other guys.

418.t: Billy Berg's club and who played there
418.s: Morgenstern mentions Dickenson's band at Billy Berg's in Los Angeles, where Hawkins, Dizzy and Charlie played.
418.q: Probably. I don't know for sure whether they played there or not. I don't know. I know Hawkins played there, and Dizzy, Charlie, and quite a few other guys.

418.t: Billy Berg's club and who played there
418.s: Morgenstern mentions Dickenson's band at Billy Berg's, where Hawkins, Dizzy and Charlie played.
418.q: Probably, I don't know for sure whether they played there or not. I know -- I know Hawkins played there and Dizzy, Charlie, and quite a few other guys.

427.t: Billy Berg's clubs in Los Angeles
427.s: He played nearly every Billy Berg club, mostly with Slam Stewart's group.
427.ch: Los Angeles scene, Tatum and Billy Berg's
427.q: I don't know...I don't know too much about Hollywood. All I know is that I would go to 'em.

427.t: The Swanee Inn in Hollywood and Slam Stewart
427.s: He worked the Swanee Inn on La Brea, where Slam Stewart and Slim Gaillard also played.
427.q: So I struggle aroun' about two years, workin' out in Hollywood. I worked for a nightclub called the Swanee Inn. Was on LaBrea. That's when I run into Slam Stewart and his group out there.

427.t: Singing after hours during 'Jump for Joy'
427.s: The Lovejoy sessions happened after the Ellington show closed each night.
427.ch: Los Angeles scene, Tatum and Billy Berg's
427.q: Yeah, it was during the period when I was working here for "Jump For Joy" with Duke Ellington's show.

169.t: The Finale Club band with Bird
169.s: McGhee's eight-piece band with four saxes including Bird, Sonny Criss and Teddy Edwards, played the Finale Club with little money.
169.ch: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
169.q: : Sonny Criss, Teddy Edwards, Gene Montgomery and Bird. So the bad was beautiful, but we weren't making any money. I mean, people would enjoy it or be loaded, but people would come into the joint that was in there before we'd come in, and we couldn't chase them out and say, "You've got to come back…

169.t: The Swing Club with Scatman Carruthers and Benny Bailey
169.s: Two months at the Swing Club, where he meets young Benny Bailey.
169.ch: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
169.q: Scatman Carruthers, and he had his band out there. He had Benny Bailey, and some cat named Sumner Smith played alto. Anyway, we were booked in there at same time, so it was a nice gig, you know.

76.t: Billy Berg's new place, the Orson Welles show and Teddy Bunn
76.s: Dance reads the biography for spring 1945, when Zutty played Berg's new club on Vine Street; they talk about Teddy Bunn, last heard with Louis Jordan's band.
76.q: Yes, that was at Billy Berg's new place. They had moved on Vine Street about this time.

76.t: After Billy Berg's: Paul Howard and a year with T-Bone Walker
76.s: After Berg's Zutty played the Streets of Paris and Swanee Inn, a night or two with Paul Howard, then a year in T-Bone Walker's band, with Mingus on bass, playing Ellington tunes at the Brown Sisters' club past Watts.
76.q: Oh yes, yes. Yes after Billy Berg's. Then I played at Streets of Paris and then we played at the Swanee Inn with Shelton Brooks, Junior, and I and Rose Murphy the Chi Chi. She was there.

105.t: Bird and Diz, Billy Berg's and the Club Capri
105.s: Hamilton says Bird and Diz were on Central Avenue at first, that Billy Berg's started later, and praises the Club Capri owner Manny and Norman Granz.
105.ch: Bebop, band changes and the road
105.q: They weren’t at Billy Berg’s at that time, they were on Central Avenue at the Downbeat, a local club, you know. Central Avenue was where all the action was.

527.t: Getting into Billy Berg's and why the Dizzy-Bird engagement failed
527.s: Farmer could not see the opening set, got in on later nights because he was tall, and says the engagement failed commercially and Bird stayed behind.
527.q: No, because I wasn’t there when the band first got on the stand ‘cause Billy Berg’s was in Hollywood, and we lived in what is called the South Central district now. We had to get a ride to go all the way out to Hollywood, and by the time we got there, they had already played a set. We just stood…

225.t: Six months at Billy Berg's in Los Angeles
225.s: The longest stay at one venue, a club where Carter's friends came, and where Bird and Diz later opened.
225.q: It could very well be. It could very well be. Another thing that stands out in my mind about the West Coast is that Benny played for almost six or eight months at a place while I was with the band in Los Angeles called Billy Berg’s Swing Club.

87.t: Working with Roy Eldridge at Billy Berg's
87.s: After a JATP tour, Young worked a few weeks at Berg's with Roy Eldridge, Anita O'Day, Willie Smith and Wardell Gray.
87.ch: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
87.q: This was in the '40's. '40. At that time I was playing with Roy Eldridge out at Billy Berg's. Me, Roy Eldridge -- Roy had the group -- Anita O'Day was singing with the group. And it's the only job I really ever worked with Roy, and the reason I worked that with him was we just came off a tour with…

88.t: The successive Billy Berg's clubs and the scale of Los Angeles music
88.s: Lee lists Billy Berg's moves from Pico and La Cienega to Beverly, Hollywood Boulevard and Vine, stressing how much music LA had.
88.ch: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
88.q: Right. Well, that was that. But I guess the point I'm really trying to make is how much music really was in Los Angeles then, and a lot of people were not aware of it;

166.t: The Spanish guitarist with Lee Young and Lester, and Billy Berg's Capri
166.s: The guitarist Louis Gonzales played with Lee and Lester; Leo Watson played at Berg's Capri.
166.ch: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
166.q: Here, when they came, to New York and played Cafe Society downtown, they played the Capri, it was -- what was the fellow's name that owned the Swing Club and the place over on Vine Street.

30.t: Billy Berg's and the small Los Angeles clubs
30.s: Billy Berg's was the best small club, with Teddy Bunn, Leo Watson, Slim Gaillard, Nellie Lutcher and Harry the Hipster Gibson.
30.q: Yeah, he's somewhere I don't know. And that's where Slim Gaillard and -- Slim and Slam, they started there.

236.t: Billy Berg's big band at the Capri and the Trouville
236.s: Billy Berg hired him for a group with Slim and Slam, Lee and Lester Young and the Spirits of Rhythm, first at the Capri and then at the Trouville.
236.ch: Billy Berg's band with Lee and Lester Young
236.q: : And finally, I got a call from Billy Berg. He wanted me to join a band with a Slim and Slam, and Lee and Lester Young, Bumps Meyers, and Jake Porter and Eddie Beal, the
